title: Complete-intersection neighbourhoods detected by the completed local ring
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $\mathfrak p\subset S$ a maximal ideal, $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $F=S/\mathfrak p$. Let $\widehat A$ be the completion at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The following are equivalent: (1) some principal affine neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$, $\operatorname{Spec}S_g$ with $g\notin\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-affine-spectrum], has coordinate algebra a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]; (2) for some integers $r,c\ge0$, $\widehat A$ is isomorphic as a ring to $F[[z_1,\ldots,z_r]]/(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$, where $h_1,\ldots,h_c$ is a regular sequence in the maximal ideal $(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. When these equivalent conditions hold, $\operatorname{depth}(A)=\dim A$ [def-weil-pbc-depth, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. In particular, if $S$ itself is a local complete intersection over $k$, then this depth equality holds at every maximal ideal.

source.place: Tags 09Q1 (lemma-quotient-regular-ring), 09Q3 (definition-lci) and 09Q6 (lemma-check-lci-agrees), combined with Algebra Tags 00SG (lemma-lci-at-prime) and 00SB (lemma-lci-CM).

proof.text: Choose a surjection $P=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to S$ from finite type, with kernel $I$, and let $\mathfrak q$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak p$. By polynomial regularity, $R=P_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local and hence Noetherian. The map $R/IR\to A$, $(u/v)\bmod IR\mapsto\bar u/\bar v$, is an isomorphism: both sides invert exactly the images of $P\setminus\mathfrak q$ in $P/I$, and their kernels are the fractions with numerator in $I$. Thus Noetherian quotients make $A$ Noetherian. Put $C=\widehat A$. By Noetherian completion and locality of completion, $C$ is Noetherian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak pAC$ and residue field $A/\mathfrak pA=F$. By completion completeness, it is $\mathfrak n$-adically complete.

source.place: 09Q6 (lemma-check-lci-agrees), proof of (1): polynomial-local presentation; Algebra 0316, 05GI and 05GG for the completion.

proof.text: The composite $k\to C\to F$ is unital, so $C\ne0$ and the map $k\to C$ is injective. Choose finitely many generators $y_i$ of $\mathfrak n$. Apply the equicharacteristic presentation lemma to obtain a surjection $\psi:Q=F[[z_1,\ldots,z_r]]\to C$ with $Q$ complete regular local and $\ker\psi\subseteq\mathfrak l=(z_i)$.

source.place: Tags 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem), part (1) and final proof paragraph, 0326 (definition-coefficient-ring), field-containing case, and 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary), first sentence; extracted from returned item steps 2 and 3.

proof.text: Assume (1). By the covering in the LCI definition, the prime of $S_g$ induced by $\mathfrak p$ belongs to some $D(a)$ with $T=(S_g)_a$ a global complete intersection. This ring is nonzero because it has that prime. Unpack its presentation $T\cong k[w_1,\ldots,w_m]/(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ with $\dim T=m-t$. Let $\mathfrak q_T$ be the prime of the polynomial ring corresponding to our point and $R_T=k[w_1,\ldots,w_m]_{\mathfrak q_T}$. By polynomial regularity, $R_T$ is regular local, and global equations says the images of the $f_i$ form a regular sequence there. The fractions identify $A\cong R_T/(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$: the elements inverted in passing from $S$ to $T$ were already outside $\mathfrak p$. Apply the completion-kernel test to this regular-local quotient and the regular-local surjection $\psi:Q\to C$ of step 2. It makes $\ker\psi$ generated by a regular sequence $h_1,\ldots,h_c$ in $\mathfrak l$. The quotient map induces the ring isomorphism $Q/(h_1,\ldots,h_c)\cong C$, proving (2).

source.place: 09Q0 (lemma-quotient-regular-ring-by-regular-sequence) and 09Q1 (lemma-quotient-regular-ring), with 09PZ; Algebra 00SB proof for regularity of the equations in a global complete intersection.

proof.text: Conversely assume (2). The ring $Q_0=F[[z_1,\ldots,z_r]]$ in that condition is regular local by power-series regularity. Composing its quotient map with the stated ring isomorphism gives a surjection $Q_0\to C$ whose kernel is generated by the given regular sequence $(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$. Apply the completion-kernel test to $R=P_{\mathfrak q}$ and $IR$ from step 1 and this surjection. It gives a regular sequence generating $IR$. By regular-kernel spreading, applied to the presentation $P/I\cong S$ at $\mathfrak p$, there is $g\notin\mathfrak p$ with $S_g$ a global complete intersection. It is a local complete intersection by the LCI definition, using the single open $D(1)$ as cover. This proves (1).

source.place: 09Q1 (lemma-quotient-regular-ring), (1) implies (2), and Algebra 00SC (lemma-lci), (5) implies (1); this is the local-to-neighbourhood passage of 00SG (lemma-lci-at-prime).

proof.text: Under (1), use $A\cong R_T/(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ from step 3. The regular-sequence quotient depth lemma gives $\operatorname{depth}A=\dim A$. If $S$ is an LCI, (1) holds with $g=1$ at every maximal ideal, proving the final assertion.
